title: A 1,600-Year-Old Man Was Found Inside a Giant Roman Jar
mediaSource: Roman dolium storage jar archaeology Bulgaria Deultum ruins ancient skeleton excavation

scenes.title: A person was found inside a giant Roman jar
scenes.narration: At the ancient Roman city of Deultum in Bulgaria, archaeologists found human remains inside a massive storage jar dating back about sixteen hundred years.

scenes.title: It was not a normal burial
scenes.narration: The remains were not found in a cemetery, but inside a defensive structure near the city's western gate. Researchers think the individual may have been a young man.

scenes.title: The area showed signs of violent destruction
scenes.narration: Ash, collapsed bricks, and melted glass were found around the jar, suggesting an intense fire and possibly an attack on the city.

scenes.title: Did he hide inside the jar?
scenes.narration: Researchers are considering whether the man climbed into the giant vessel to hide during an attack by groups such as Germanic tribes or the Huns.
keywords: Roman dolium large storage jar museum

scenes.title: He may never have escaped
scenes.narration: The position of the skeleton does not clearly suggest an attempt to climb out. Smoke, heat, and fire around the structure may have trapped him inside.

scenes.title: A storage jar may have become a final refuge
scenes.narration: An ordinary Roman storage jar may have become one person's last hiding place. Sixteen centuries later, archaeology is revealing that final moment again.
